questions.question: Explain why an electric circuit is called a system. Describe its input, process and output.
questions.expected_answer: A system is a set of parts that work together to do a job, and a circuit's parts work together to transfer energy. The input is energy from an energy source such as a cell or battery. The process is the transfer of electrical energy through conducting wires. The output is the useful job done by the device, such as light from a bulb, sound from a buzzer or movement from a motor.

questions.question: Name the three components every working circuit needs and say what each does.
questions.expected_answer: An energy source, such as a cell or battery, which stores energy and releases it as electrical energy. Conducting wires, usually copper covered in plastic, which carry the electricity from the source to the device and back. A device, such as a bulb, buzzer, motor or heater, which changes electrical energy into a useful form.

questions.question: Trace the energy in a circuit with a cell and a motor.
questions.expected_answer: The energy starts as chemical energy stored in the cell. It is transferred as electrical energy through the wires to the motor. The motor changes it into movement energy, as the propeller turns, with some heat and sound. The energy is not used up; it is changed into other forms, and the cell slowly goes flat.
